clue.text: Brief outfit for a special figure

definitions.note: a prime number is a figure with special properties, divisible only by itself and one

parts.note: to brief someone is to prime them with information
a number is an item of clothing, as in 'a little black number'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a skimpy outfit to wear for a special figure, perhaps a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief outfit' looks like skimpy clothing, but 'Brief' is a verb here: to brief someone is to prime them.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime number is divisible only by one and itself, which makes it a mathematically distinctive figure.

clue.text: Correspondence from Proust to be regularly at gallery from the start

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Proust to be, starting with the first
from the start means taking the opening letter of each of the words at and gallery

explanation.surface: Letters from the novelist Proust, to be shown at an art gallery from the opening day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes P, O, S, T, B from PROUSTTOBE; 'from the start' gives A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the collection of letters a person or publication receives, so it stands for correspondence.

clue.text: Steamed up in refitted frigate — leaders of force getting withheld

indicators.note: a ship that is refitted has its parts reworked, so the letters are rearranged
withheld means these letters are kept out of the word frigate
leaders of means the first letters of the words force and getting

explanation.surface: Sailors are angry in a refitted warship because the top brass of the navy are holding back pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' gives F and G, which 'withheld' removes from FRIGATE to leave RIATE; 'refitted' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steamed up is an idiom for being angry, the same feeling as irate.

clue.text: Weakness of vision in Spain agreed with court

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
yes is what you say when you have agreed
a court is a royal retinue, and a train is the procession of attendants following a monarch

explanation.surface: An ailment of the eyes noticed in Spain, settled by a court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' here is the monarch's attendants, not a law court or a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness of the eyes from overuse, a temporary weakening of sight.

clue.text: Ship's doctor, where child needs amputation, is prompt

indicators.note: amputation is a cutting off, so these letters are cut away from the doctor

parts.note: a ship's surgeon is the doctor aboard
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A naval surgeon finds a child needs a limb removed and is quick to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs amputation' cuts SON out of SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to urge them on, push them to act.

clue.text: The setter is able to sit below Sting in concert hall

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that sits below another follows it

parts.note: a barb is a sharp sting, as on a hook or a remark
the setter refers to themself as I
can means is able

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter can sit below the rock star Sting at a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' looks like the singer, but it means a barb. The Barbican is a London arts centre with a major concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbican Centre in London houses a famous concert venue, home to the London Symphony Orchestra.

clue.text: Survey playground underwritten by church

indicators.note: in a down answer, something underwritten has the next piece written beneath it

parts.note: a rec is a British recreation ground, a public playing field
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A survey of a playground, with the church underwriting the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwritten' looks financial, but it places CE below REC. A rec is a British public park or playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a preliminary inspection of an area.

clue.text: Mum quiet, only coming upstairs — something's brewing here!

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming upstairs means reading from bottom to top, so this word is reversed

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Mum, keep quiet; only come upstairs, there's something brewing in here!
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming upstairs' reverses BUT to TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A mash tub is the vessel in which malt and hot water are mixed when brewing beer.

clue.text: Dam, some say, with northward current — it's monstrous!

indicators.note: some say signals the word is to be heard, with a sound-alike spelling entered

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

indicators.note: in a down answer, going northward means reading upwards, so this word is reversed

parts.note: a flow is a current

explanation.surface: A dam with the river current running north is a monstrous thing.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIR sounds like WERE for those who pronounce it so; 'northward' reverses FLOW to WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a mythical creature, a person turned into a wolf, so it is a monster.

clue.text: He rakes in shattered crags, even

indicators.note: rocks shattered into pieces suggest letters broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man rakes about among broken crags, even so.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger searches through refuse to collect what is usable, raking among leftovers.

clue.text: Champs elect to be heard

definitions.note: champs is a verb, he or she champs

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is spoken and a sound-alike spelling entered

parts.note: to elect is to choose

explanation.surface: Sporting champions choose to make themselves heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champs' looks like champions, but it is the verb meaning to chomp.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch noisily, as a horse does on its bit, the same as chewing.

clue.text: Slight suspicion about entering sauna, say?

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sauna is an example of a bath, a steam bath
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A faint suspicion about someone going into the sauna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sauna as one example of a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath of scandal is a mere hint or whisper of it, so a breath is a slight suspicion.

clue.text: Support when traversing choppy Elbe?

indicators.note: traversing means stretching across, so this word is placed around the other

parts.note: a lift is a support that raises something

indicators.note: choppy water is rough and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something to keep you afloat when crossing the rough waters of the River Elbe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elbe is a German river; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since the device is a support for anyone crossing choppy water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a floating ring that keeps a swimmer up, a support for anyone crossing rough water.

clue.text: Cheering news — one's gaining a pound …

indicators.note: gaining means adding the following pieces on

parts.note: gen is slang for information or news
one's is one is, and one is I, the Roman numeral
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from libra

explanation.surface: The cheering news is that one is gaining a pound in weight, or money.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 15 Across, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means cheerful and friendly, the manner of someone in good spirits.

clue.text: Follow directions audibly from labourer on step

indicators.note: audibly means the words are said out loud and a sound-alike spelling entered

parts.note: a navvy is a labourer, and a gait is a step or walk; on puts one after the other

explanation.surface: Follow the instructions given out loud by a workman standing on a step.
explanation.walkthrough: NAVVY is a British word for a manual labourer digging roads or canals.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plot or follow a route, working out which way to go.

clue.text: … towards a curry, perhaps, after Charlie's underground excavation

indicators.note: after means these pieces follow the first

parts.note: Charlie is the radio alphabet word for C
at can mean towards, as in aiming at
to curry a horse is to groom it, one way to comb it

explanation.surface: Following on from good news, someone heads off towards a curry after Charlie's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like a meal, but it is the verb for grooming a horse with a curry comb.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber cut into rock, a man-made subterranean excavation.

clue.text: His out-tray, not small, could be specialist

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word
not means this letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An expert's in-tray and out-tray, his out-tray not being a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not small' removes an S from HISOUTTRAY, and 'could be' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority is an expert on a subject, someone whose specialist knowledge is relied upon.

clue.text: American skipper of Nautilus, on three points, displaying bloomers

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the piece follows

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel
N, E and S are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: An American captain of a submarine, on three counts, is caught showing his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like old-fashioned underwear, but it means plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Envy about Granny's engagement

indicators.note: about means this word goes around the other

parts.note: to covet is to envy
nan is a familiar word for granny

explanation.surface: Someone is jealous of grandmother's engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a binding agreement, a formal commitment of the kind an engagement makes.

clue.text: Shelters accommodate fifty per cent of rides in characteristic groups

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so these letters are put inside the shelters

parts.note: cots, or cotes, are small shelters for animals

indicators.note: fifty per cent of means keeping only the first half of the word and cutting the rest

parts.note: horses are rides, animals ridden

explanation.surface: Shelters take in half the fairground rides for groups of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty per cent of' takes HOR, the first half of HORSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a set of people sharing a defining trait, such as those born in the same year.

clue.text: Gobbles very loudly in street beside The Telegraph

indicators.note: beside means these two pieces sit side by side
in means this piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the newspaper refers to itself as us
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone noisily wolfs food in the street next to the newspaper's office.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in the Telegraph, so 'The Telegraph' is US.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to gobble greedily, eating too much too fast.

clue.text: Son cunning about feet being fast

indicators.note: about means this word goes around the other

parts.note: wily means cunning

explanation.surface: A crafty son is fleet of foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftly means quickly, at speed, the adverb sense of fast.

clue.text: Up-tempo shindig?

parts.note: up means high
tempo is the time of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A lively, fast-paced party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a shindig is one kind of high time, a lively celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A high time is a spell of lively merrymaking, which a rowdy party provides.

clue.text: Drone with loose filament

definitions.meaning: to make a monotonous humming sound
a loose thread or fringe left at the end of a weaver's warp

explanation.surface: A buzzing insect trailing a loose strand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrum is both a steady humming noise and a weaver's word for a dangling end of thread.

clue.text: Small-scale plant's into carbon sailing-boats

definitions.note: plant's is plant is, the definition joined to the rest by is

indicators.note: into means the answer is tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: A miniature plant is somehow used in making carbon sailing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai are trees grown in pots and kept dwarfed by pruning, plants in miniature.

clue.text: Singular source for expansion

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: One unique cause behind a growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a rise or increase in size, an expansion like a swelling wave.

clue.text: Kind of arch exclamations?

definitions.meaning: an arch shaped by two S-curves meeting at a point
O and GEE are two exclamations of surprise, together read as the answer

explanation.surface: People gasp at a type of arch.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is a pointed arch of double curves common in Gothic buildings; split, it reads O, GEE.

clue.text: Aerofoil allowing forward or backward movement and view?

definitions.text: Aerofoil allowing forward or backward movement and view?

indicators.text: forward or backward movement and view?
indicators.note: a word that gives the same view read forward or backward is a palindrome, as this one is

parts.note: an aerofoil is a wing-shaped surface; a helicopter's spinning blade assembly is one

explanation.surface: A wing section that lets a craft move forward or back and gives a good view.
explanation.walkthrough: Helicopter blades let the craft move forward or backward; the 'view' hint is that the word reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor blade is a rotating aerofoil, the wing-like surface that lifts a helicopter.

clue.text: Without ceremony, nightdress is trimmed by South Bank playhouse

indicators.note: by means the next piece sits beside the first
trimmed means a letter is cut off the end of the word

parts.note: a negligee is a light nightdress
NT is the National Theatre, on London's South Bank

explanation.surface: Wearing a cut-down nightie informally beside a South Bank theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Theatre stands on the South Bank of the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent can mean careless or casual in manner, so it fits acting without formality or ceremony.

clue.text: Sly army type misused component of a cycle from York

definitions.text: component of a cycle from York

indicators.note: letters that are misused are put to the wrong use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cunning soldier was misused in a play from York.
explanation.walkthrough: The York Mystery Plays are a medieval cycle of Bible dramas still staged in York.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery play is a medieval religious drama, performed in sequences such as the York cycle.
